title: $1 million, but no phone ever — Part 2
style: Warm painterly 2D cartoon illustration, cinematic graphic-novel look: clean bold dark outlines, rich textured digital painting, soft volumetric light, deep warm oranges and moody blues, detailed environment, vertical 9:16 composition.
character: MAIN CHARACTER: a lanky ADULT man drawn as a minimalist cartoon: a perfectly round smooth tan head, two tiny solid black dot eyes set wide apart, short thin eyebrow strokes, a very small simple mouth, no nose, no visible hair, simple long limbs, dark charcoal baseball cap, oversized heather-grey hoodie, black slim pants, white sneakers. Minimal face like a webcomic, not a child, not anime, no big eyes.

scenes.A: The man shaking hands with a mysterious man in a dark suit across a cafe table, a briefcase of cash between them, decision made.
scenes.B: The man at a bank counter talking to a friendly teller, handing over an ID card, bright bank interior, no readable text.
scenes.C: The man walking through a park with a paper map and a small notebook, friends waving at him from a bench, autumn leaves.
scenes.D: The man at a cozy dinner table with friends laughing, no phones on the table, candles, warm light.
scenes.E: Close-up portrait of the man facing the viewer, calm content smile, park in sunlight behind him.

segments.text: The catch was that the bank needs a phone to log in. So you walk into a branch with your ID instead.
Week one is chaos. You get lost twice. You miss a party.
Week four, your friends start showing up at your door instead of texting.
Month six. You sleep eight hours. You notice everything.
A year later, the stranger asks if you regret it.
You don't. The million was nice. Getting your time back was the real prize. The end.
